segments.expected: What was nearest to a cask full of water, it turned out, was a cask full of water. The Company's cooper sent it down from the yard behind the Long Quay on a dray: a brewer's tun with eight iron hoops, as wide across as a big man is tall, standing on end with no head in it. Boards had been nailed across its bottom from the outside, because a tun with no head and no bottom would not have held a cupful. They lowered it down the Graving's ramp on rollers and stood it on the stone of the dock floor at the seaward end, on the chalk where the lane pen had been, and the Company's men filled it from the fire main with a canvas hose until the water stood in it level with the top hoop. "It's not right," said Brask, looking at it. "It's got a bottom."
